Mahbubey Alam, Additional Attorney-General, instructed by Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record------For the Appellant. 
Mainul Hosein, Advocate, instructed by Md Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record------For the Respondent.
parties:
State ------ Appellant
Vs.
Faisal Alam Ansari ------ Respondent.
full_judgment:
Latifur Rahman CJ: This appeal by the State-appellant is against the judgment and order dated 9-8-2000 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2741 of 2000 making the Rule absolute granting bail to accused-respondent Faisal Alam Ansari. 

 3. The accused respondent unsuccessfully prayed for bail before the Courts below. Thereafter in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2741 of 2000, a Division Bench of the High Court Division made the Rule absolute and granted bail to the accused-respondent on condition that he would surrender his international passport to the Deputy Commissioner prior to submission of his bail bond. 

 5. It appears from the judgment of the High Court Division that the first information report was made within three hours of the occurrence wherein the accused-respondent Faisal Alam Ansari was mentioned as the main accused along with others. It is also found from the record that driver Rahim recognised the accused in the TI Parade. Although subsequently he made contradictory statements about recognition of the accused in the TI Parade and had sworn an affidavit before the Notary Public. The truth or falsity of this document will be gone into at the trial. This affidavit cannot have any bearing at the present moment in considering the question of bail of toe accused-respondent. Further, we also find that the accused-respondent was found last in the company of the deceased just 45 minutes before the occurrence and this statement was also supported by other witnesses in their statements under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. That apart, in the first information report there is also mention of clear motive of the murder. By now police has submitted charge sheet against the accused under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and the Case records has already been transmitted in the Court of Metropolitan Sessions Judge for trial and next date has been fixed for framing of the charge on 19-11-2000 In the facts and circumstances of the case we hold that the learned Judges of the High Court Division did not exercise their judicial discretion in granting bail to the accused. 

 6. Mr Mainul Hosein, learned Advocate appearing for the accused-respondent, submits that there is no eye-witness of the occurrence and the chance of false implication cannot be altogether ruled out in this particular case. 

 7. At this stage we are only considering the question of bail and, as such, we should confine ourselves only with the available materials that has been produced by the prosecution to show the implication of the accused with the alleged murder, where we find reasonable grounds for believing that the accused is guilty of the offence which is punishable with death or imprisonment for life. We find a strong prima facie case for not granting bail. 

 10. This means the personal liberty of a person can be deprived if law permits that. Here in this case the primary allegations against the accused is that he had committed an offence of murder for which charge sheet has been submitted under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code. Section 497 of the Code of Criminal Procedure speaks that when there is a reasonable ground for believing that a person is guilty of offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, he should not be granted bail. Section 497 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is a procedural law and the accused having alleged to have committed a substantive offence of murder his liberty is curtailed. In that view of the matter the argument with regard to violation of fundamental right cannot be accepted in the facts of the present case as law permits of such arrest and detention in custody. Article 33 of our Constitution speaks of safe guard as to arrest and detention. Here arrest in reality means arrest in connection with criminal offence and the word detention is used in the sense of preventive detention as will be evident from reading the foregoing clauses of Article 33. Strictly speaking, the accused respondent is arrested for committing an alleged criminal offence. We are to decide whether there is any law authorising such deprivation of liberty of a person not beyond that. Thus the argument of Mainul Hosein on the ground of violation of fundamental right cannot be accepted. I may also point out here that "save in accordance with law" as mentioned in Article 32 not only refers to criminal law but also civil law which provides for arrest and detention, namely, for recovery of decretal dues and public dues. Consequently, the submission of Mr Mainul Hosein on the ground of violation of fundamental right is totally misconceived as law provides for such arrest.
